title: Platform systems & services: integrated playbook, dashboards, runbooks, roadmap and team wiki
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates the Platform team’s canonical guidance for systems and services ownership, dashboards & alerts, operational runbooks, retrospective actions, and the near-term roadmap. It is intended as the single-entry reference for on-call engineers, platform owners, and new team members.

Sections in this document:
- Ownership and service map
- Dashboards & alerting standards
- Key runbooks (incident triage, capacity, rollback)
- How-tos and contribution guidelines
- Q1 retrospective and action items
- Roadmap and upcoming priorities
- Team wiki & onboarding checklist

1) Ownership and service map
- Primary services: control-plane-api, routing-proxy, batch-batcher, kv-cache, telemetry-ingest, model-router, autoscaler.
- Owners (primary / secondary): control-plane-api: Platform API (J. Rios / D. Martinez); routing-proxy: Edge (P. Singh / M. Zhou); batch-batcher: Serving Runtime (S. Patel / L. Nguyen).
- On-call rotations: platform-oncall (2wk cadence), infra-oncall (2wk cadence). PagerDuty schedules and escalation policies are in the team wiki.

2) Dashboards & alerting standards
- Dashboard naming: platform.<service>.<view> (e.g., platform.control-plane-api.latency).
- Dashboards to maintain (minimum):
  - control-plane-api: 50/95/99 latency, request rate, 5xx rate, error budget consumption.
  - model-router: queue depth, avg batch-size, dropped-requests, routing-fallbacks.
  - batch-batcher: batch latency, GPU utilization, backpressure rate.
  - telemetry-ingest: ingest rate, failed-events, retention lag.
- Standard alert thresholds (examples):
  - control-plane-api: P95 latency > 300ms for 5m -> SEV2; error rate > 1% for 5m -> SEV1.
  - model-router queue depth > 1000 for 10m -> SEV2; dropped-requests > 100/5m -> SEV1.
  - GPU utilization > 95% for 10m and queue depth increasing -> capacity-warning (SEV3).
- Alert structure: title, impacted service, symptom, runbook link, owner, PagerDuty severity, slack channel. All new alerts require a short rationale and estimated noise-rate.

3) Key runbooks (summary & links)
- Incident triage (platform-incident-runbook): 1) acknowledge in PagerDuty, 2) open incident doc, 3) collect dashboard links, 4) run initial metrics queries, 5) isolate service/component, 6) mitigation, 7) postmortem assignment.
- Rapid rollback (deployment-rollback-runbook): criteria for rollback, how to trigger previous image, DB migration guardrails, communication checklist.
- Capacity scaling (scale-up-playbook): steps to add GPU pool, update autoscaler policy, verify model-variants compatibility, and run load smoke tests.
- Degraded-mode routing (graceful-degradation): policy for routing to cheaper/compatible model variants when capacity constrained, configuration examples, and telemetry to monitor quality impact.

4) How-tos and contribution guidelines
- Adding a dashboard: create a panel under platform.<service>.<view>, include metric description, owner, and expected ranges. Submit PR to dashboards repo and tag reviewers (oncall, service owner).
- Creating a new alert: open an issue with the alert JSON + rationale, expected false-positive rate, mitigation steps, owner. Alert must be reviewed by oncall and a secondary owner before enabling in prod.
- Onboarding a new service to platform: complete the Service Readiness checklist (API contract, health endpoints, metrics, docs, canaries, runbook). Checklist link is in team wiki.
- Updating runbooks: all runbooks are in the runbooks repo. Edit and open PR; include a test plan or tabletop notes for significant changes.

5) Q1 2026 retrospective (high level)
- Summary: Q1 incidents were dominated by two classes: model-router queuing regressions (3 incidents) and control-plane API deploy-related errors (2 incidents). Both were mitigated quickly but contributed to SLO burn.
- Root causes identified: incomplete autoscaler config for lambda-like traffic spikes; insufficient deploy-time validation for config-driven feature flags.
- Action items (status):
  1. Autoscaler policy revamp and canary for burst traffic (owner: S. Patel) — in progress, target complete 2026-02-28.
  2. Add deploy-time configuration validation in CI for control-plane (owner: P. Singh) — done 2026-01-12.
  3. Improve queue-depth dashboards and add early-warning alerts (owner: D. Martinez) — in progress.

6) Roadmap (next 3 quarters priorities)
- Q2 2026: finish autoscaler policy rollout; standardize dashboard templates and reduce alert noise by 30%; launch platform self-serve canaries.
- Q3 2026: implement cross-region fallback routing; add model-quality telemetry tied to canaries; integrate cost-per-token dashboards.
- Q4 2026: formalize compliance runbooks for Private deployments and expand observability retention for enterprise customers.

7) Team wiki & onboarding checklist (quick links)
- Links: Service readiness checklist | PagerDuty schedules | Dashboards repo | Runbooks repo | Incident doc template.
- New hire checklist (platform eng):
  - Access: ensure access to Grafana, Prometheus, PagerDuty, Slack channels.
  - Read: this playbook, recent retrospectives, incident postmortems for the last 6 months.
  - Hands-on: run a tabletop incident drill, submit a dashboard PR, and shadow oncall twice.

Appendices
- Example alert JSON (text):
{
  "title": "control-plane-api: high p95 latency",
  "expr": "histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service)) > 0.3",
  "for": "5m",
  "severity": "sev2",
  "owner": "platform-api@redwood.ai",
  "runbook": "/confluence/eng-platform/platform-incident-runbook-2026-q1"
}

- Contacts & escalation: primary oncall (platform-oncall), secondary infra-oncall, SRE lead (Diego Martinez), Platform eng manager (Ava Chen).

If you are the owner of a service or a runbook referenced here, validate the entries annually and when significant architecture changes occur. For questions or suggested updates, open a PR in the runbooks repo and ping #platform-runbooks on Slack.
